initialize.instructions:
Call repowise first for where/how/why questions about this repo's code.
- search_codebase(query) finds an identifier or literal: `lines` are read from live files; `complete: true` means every match.
- get_context(targets=[symbol], include=["references"]) before a rename: a `complete` list is the whole edit set. include=["files"] on a directory lists its files and tests.
- get_answer(question): one how/where/why question per call.
- get_why before changing an established pattern.
- No decisions recorded yet: get_why reads git history and code comments.
Agent note, not for answers: setup unfinished. If the user is still chatting, offer `repowise next --prompt setup` once; declined: `repowise next --dismiss setup`.

tools.name: get_answer
tools.description:
Answer a how, where, or why question in one evidence-grounded call.

High confidence may be used directly; medium and low lead with the
evidence to verify. `candidate_files` ranks files worth opening that
the citations do not name.

question.description: One question about one subject; split a multi-part task.

scope.description: Repository-relative path prefix; several, comma-separated, search their union.

tools.name: get_context
tools.description:
Triage card for files, modules or symbols: relationships, not source bytes.

Returns summary, signatures with lines, hotspot, fix_history and
decision titles; either risk cue means get_risk. Batch targets in one
call. Whole file, body-elided and line-verified: include=["skeleton"]
in ONE call, or Read it; do not call get_symbol per signature. Rename:
include=["references"] is the whole edit set when `complete`. Which
files in a directory lack tests: include=["files"] on it.

include.description: callers | callees | references | skeleton | files | symbols | decisions | full_doc | ownership | last_change | health | doc_drift | changes | suspects (pass symptom=).

tools.name: get_symbol
tools.description:
Follow-up read of one symbol whose id another response already gave you.

**Not an entry point.** `get_answer` ships `symbol_bodies`; for a
whole file `get_context(include=["skeleton"])` or a Read is one call.
Never walk a file symbol by symbol. Returns verified, line-numbered
source; a truncated result carries the `continuation` to pass back as
symbol_id.

symbol_id.description: "path/to/file.py::Name", "path/to/file.py:140-180" for a live range, or an omission ref.

query.description: Regex or substring filter on an omission ref's lines.

depth.description: 1 is this symbol alone; 2-3 also return the bodies it calls, transitively, in `callee_bodies`.

tools.name: get_why
tools.description:
Why this code is shaped this way: decision records and evidence commits.

Call before a refactor or pattern divergence. A path gets the rules in
force first, then labelled background records. `authority: accepted`
means somebody signed the decision; `answer_basis` names the strongest
evidence lane, and only `decision` is a ruling.

query.description: A question, a file or module path, or omit for the decision dashboard.

targets.description: File paths to anchor a question.

id.description: Decision or `ev_...` evidence id from any tool.

include.description: ["history"]: a path's origin story, commits, episodes.

tools.name: search_codebase
tools.description:
Find code by concept, symbol, or path: hybrid codebase search.

For a how/where/why question call get_answer. Use this to enumerate
matches, resolve an identifier to a symbol_id, or find files for
get_context. Identifier, literal, `a|b|c` or regex queries return
`lines` (path, line, kind, text; definitions first, one group per
alternative; `in` names the enclosing symbol until it changes) read
from live files; when `complete` is true they are every match, so no
grep is needed. `candidates` lists distinct files to Read, best first.

query.description: Identifier, `a|b` alternation, regex, path, or natural language.
